label: Fed Funds Rate
value: 3.50–3.75%; September 15-16 Hike Odds ~83-87% as Oman-Hosted Hormuz Talks Collapse and the 10-Year Yield Nears 5% Two Days Before the Decision
source: Federal Reserve FOMC, July 29 2026 (held); BLS PPI (Sept 10) and CPI (Sept 11) August releases; CME FedWatch, Sept 14 2026; Bloomberg / NPR / Al Jazeera, Sept 14 2026
delta: Little changed from Sept 11 (~87%) — Monday's collapse of the Oman-hosted Hormuz talks and a fresh oil surge keep the hike case intact into the Sept 15-16 meeting
deltaNote: SEPT 8-11 ARC: Canada's $27.6B retaliatory tariffs took effect Sept 8, adding a fresh trade-friction input. The Aug PPI (Sept 10) showed wholesale inflation accelerating to 5.4% YoY, over three-quarters of the rise from energy (diesel +24.1%) as the Gulf oil shock fed into producer prices; the 10Y Treasury hit a 4.969% cycle high the same day as Brent topped $105-107, its highest in nearly four months. The Aug CPI (Sept 11) then ran hot on core — 0.3% MoM (0.1pp above forecast), 2.4% YoY in line — even though headline (3.4% YoY, 0.4% MoM) matched consensus. CME FedWatch hike odds for the Sept 15-16 FOMC jumped to ~87% (from ~70% pre-CPI), with Nationwide's Kathy Bostjancic noting Warsh's condition for a hold — continued disinflation — was not met. Equities rallied Sept 11 (Dow +1.03%, S&P +1.07%, Nasdaq +1.23%) as oil pulled back, ending a four-session slide. SEPT 12-13 WEEKEND: With cash markets shut, the story shifted to diplomacy and the Gulf itself — the UAE's Crown Prince met Iran's Pezeshkian at the BRICS summit Sept 12 (first high-level UAE-Iran contact since Abu Dhabi's August trade suspension), and Iran signaled a shared Hormuz shipping route with Oman was close to signing. That diplomatic thaw was undercut hours later: a still-unclaimed strike killed one crew member on a vessel near Qeshm/Hengam Island on Sept 13, with shipping through the strait now running roughly 90% below its pre-conflict baseline. SEPT 14 (MONDAY REOPEN): The Salalah meeting between Iran, Iraq and GCC states meant to set up a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor was postponed at Saudi Arabia's request after Houthi forces seized Yemen's Red Sea port of Mokha over the weekend and struck Saudi territory again — Oman's FM Badr Albusaidi said the delay was 'in the interests of consensus.' Oil futures jumped over 3% at the open (Brent to $108.23, WTI to $103.20) and the 10-year Treasury yield touched an intraday high near 5.00% — its highest since October 2023 — before easing; the S&P 500 closed down 0.35% at 7,630.34. CME FedWatch odds for the Sept 15-16 hike held at roughly 83-87% heading into Wednesday's decision and Chair Warsh's press conference. Prior: Waller's Sept 3 dovish remarks briefly cut odds to ~48-55%; the Sept 4 jobs blowout (+162K vs +53K expected) reversed that to ~58%.

deltaNote: SEPT 4-10 ARC: The Sept 4 jobs blowout sent the 10Y back to 4.79%, near its Sept 2 cycle high, as CME hike odds rose to ~58%. Yields kept climbing into the new week: a fourth straight losing session for stocks on Sept 9 came alongside the 10Y touching its highest level since 2023 even after Treasury Secretary Bessent unveiled a $6B bond buyback plan aimed at supporting liquidity. The move culminated Sept 10 when the Aug PPI showed wholesale inflation accelerating to 5.4% YoY (energy +4.2%, diesel +24.1%) on the Gulf conflict's oil shock — the same day Brent topped $105-107/bbl (highest in ~4 months) and diesel hit a record $5.94/gal — sending the 10Y to roughly 4.97%, its firmest level since October 2023. The Sept 11 CPI (core 0.3% MoM, hot) pushed Fed hike odds to ~87%, though yields eased modestly as oil pulled back and stocks rallied. The 30-year's Aug 17 peak of 5.31-5.32% (highest since June 2007) remains the cycle high for that tenor. National debt concerns (nearing $40T), stubborn above-target inflation, and the unresolved US-Iran Gulf conflict remain the structural floor under long-end yields heading into the Sept 15-16 FOMC. SEPT 14 (MONDAY): The Salalah meeting meant to set up a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor was postponed after Saudi Arabia objected to its wording amid fresh Houthi attacks on its territory and the seizure of Yemen's Red Sea port of Mokha over the weekend. Oil jumped over 3% at the open (Brent $108.23, WTI $103.20) and the 10Y touched an intraday high near 5.00% — its highest since October 2023 — two days before the Fed's decision, before easing slightly as stocks closed only modestly lower (S&P 500 -0.35% to 7,630.34).

deltaNote: AUG 2026 FINAL (released Aug 28): 51.7, revised up from the 51.0 preliminary but still down 6.3% from July's final 55.2 and roughly 11% below a year ago.
